properties.name: anchor
properties.description: ID of the anchor element to position relative to.

properties.name: placement
properties.description: Position of the menu relative to the anchor.

properties.name: variant
properties.description:
Visual variant.
- 'baseline': MD3 baseline menu (square corners, surface container)
- 'standard': M3 Expressive vertical menu (rounded, surface-based colors)
- 'vibrant': M3 Expressive vertical menu (rounded, tertiary-based colors)

properties.name: layout
properties.description: Layout style for vertical menus. 'standard' is flat, 'grouped' uses visual section separators.

properties.name: useGap
properties.description: Use gap separators instead of dividers between groups (vertical menu only).

properties.name: emptyText
properties.description: Message shown when all menu items are hidden (e.g. no filter results). Empty string disables.

properties.name: matchAnchorWidth
properties.description: When true, the menu surface min-width matches the anchor element's width. The menu still grows wider if items need more space.

properties.name: responsive
properties.description:
Adapt to compact viewports. The menu is *always* clamped within the
viewport (it never overflows the screen and pins to the edges with a
margin). When `responsive` is set, on viewports at or below the compact
breakpoint (600px) the menu additionally expands to near-full-width
below the trigger for comfortable touch use.

properties.name: persistent
properties.description:
When set, the menu does NOT auto-dismiss in response to interaction
elsewhere on the page. By default a menu closes when:
  1. The user clicks outside the menu and its anchor.
  2. Another non-persistent menu opens (single-open coordination —
     opening menu B closes menu A so two top-level menus never
     overlap each other on screen).

`persistent` opts out of both auto-dismiss paths. The menu then only
closes via `close()`, the anchor's toggle, item activation, or
Escape. Useful for modal-style pickers, multi-step menus, and any
context where the consumer manages dismissal explicitly.

Submenus (an `<md-menu>` rendered inside a parent menu's `submenu`
slot) are never affected by sibling-menu dismissal even without this
flag — ancestors and descendants are always preserved.

properties.name: autoFocus
properties.description:
When false, opening the menu initializes roving tabindex without moving
focus to the first item. The consumer handles focus (e.g. docked pickers
that scroll to the selected option). `show({ autoFocus: false })` still
takes precedence for a single open.

properties.name: maxHeight
properties.description:
Cap the menu surface block-size. When the items exceed it the list
scrolls vertically inside a plain scroll viewport. A number is treated
as pixels; any CSS length is passed through (e.g. `'50vh'`). Unset, the
cap falls back to `--md-menu-max-block-size` (250px). Applies to menus
with submenus too: their flyouts are `position: fixed` and escape the
scroll viewport rather than being clipped by it.

properties.name: listbox
properties.description:
Present the popup as a WAI-ARIA listbox (surface `role="presentation"`,
anchor `aria-haspopup="listbox"`) rather than a menu. `md-select` sets this
for both its virtual and non-virtual lists so the popup is a listbox of
options regardless of size. (The virtual path additionally registers a
provider, which adds the aria-activedescendant focus model.)

properties.name: density
properties.description:
Local density rung. Drives the same `--md-sys-density-scale` signal that a
global `data-density` ancestor sets, so a local value simply overrides the
inherited one. 0 = default, -4 = ultra-compact.

cssProperties.name: --md-menu-max-block-size
cssProperties.description: Max height before the list scrolls (default 250px);

cssProperties.name: --md-menu-inline-fill-radius-end
cssProperties.description: Bottom corner radius for inline-fill embed (default 0)

name: Menu
description: A temporary set of actions or options, anchored to a trigger. Handles placement, viewport flipping and clamping, roving focus, typeahead and dismissal. It is also the dropdown surface inside md-select, md-multi-select, md-autocomplete and md-date-picker.

notes: Dedicated native renderer (SwiftUI / Compose): the baseline, standard and vibrant surfaces, the standard and grouped (gap) layouts, the header slot, empty text, density, a capped scrolling viewport (max-height, --md-menu-max-block-size) and the 150 ms scale-and-fade entrance and exit (quick and Reduce Motion snap), verified against the Mac Chrome 153 oracles (paint, interaction states and motion).

Anchored menus present in the nearest AWCMenuScope (the menus' top layer): bottom/top-start/end placement against the anchor's live frame (physical, as the source), flipped and kept inside the viewport margin, match-anchor-width and the responsive full-width surface. Outside a scope a menu renders in flow.

Source behaviour: auto-focus of the first row, roving focus with typeahead, Escape and Tab close the tree and restore focus to the anchor, outside clicks close non-persistent menus, opening a menu closes its open peers; mdOpen / mdClose as the source. listbox exposes the surface as a listbox of options.

show({ autoFocus }), close(), whenClosed() and reposition() through AWCMenuScopeState.menu(id); getScrollViewport() returns the viewport geometry (scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight) rather than an element. setComboboxElement() and setVirtualProvider() are the DOM combobox and virtualization plumbing of md-select / md-autocomplete and have no native counterpart.
The six menu hooks and the five row hooks (inherited by every row) through .awcMenuAppearance(…) / AWCMenuAppearanceScope.
